one_line_purpose: This project implements a FastAPI-based audio analysis service that uploads audio files, extracts relevant features, performs similarity search, and supports mood-based natural language search.
problem_solved: It addresses the need for quick retrieval and mood-based search within music or audio datasets by providing a REST API to analyze, store, and search audio files based on their acoustic features and metadata.
architecture_summary: The project is a REST API built using FastAPI. It uses an SQLite database (managed by SQLAlchemy) to store audio metadata (title, tags) and extracted acoustic features (tempo, spectral centroid, RMS, duration, ZCR, rolloff). Audio files are uploaded via a POST endpoint and stored locally on the filesystem. Upon upload, librosa is used to extract features. The API provides endpoints for similarity search against an existing audio ID (using Euclidean or Cosine distance on normalized feature vectors), search by feature ranges, text search by title or tags, and a mood-based natural language search that categorizes audio based on feature thresholds.
key_features: Audio file upload and local storage (supports .wav, .mp3)
Extraction of core audio features (tempo, spectral centroid, RMS, duration, zero-crossing rate, spectral rolloff) using librosa
Storage of extracted features and metadata in an SQLite database
Similarity search between audio tracks based on features (cosine or Euclidean distance)
Search by specified feature ranges (e.g., tempo, RMS)
Text search by audio title or tags
Mood-based natural language search by mapping audio features to descriptive labels
Normalization of feature vectors before similarity computation
Collision-safe file saving for uploaded audio files
Result limiting to top 5 for similarity searches
notable_code_decisions: Utilizes FastAPI for API development, SQLAlchemy for ORM with SQLite, and librosa for audio processing.
Features are normalized using z-score (mean-standard deviation) before similarity calculations.
Supports both cosine similarity and Euclidean distance as configurable metrics for audio similarity search.
Implements a mechanism to prevent file overwrites by appending an index to filenames during upload.
Mood-based search uses predefined thresholds on raw features (tempo, RMS, spectral centroid) to assign qualitative labels.
Features are stored as individual columns (Float type) in the SQLite database rather than a single JSON blob.
Text search provides a basic ranking by counting matches in title and tags.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: Feature extraction relies on basic librosa features; advanced techniques like pre-trained embeddings (e.g., PANNs, OpenL3, MusiCNN) are explicitly not used, limiting the richness of audio representation.
Mood inference is based on simple thresholding of a few features, which may not capture complex musical emotions accurately.
Audio files and metadata are stored locally in a SQLite database and filesystem, making the solution less scalable for large-scale, distributed deployments.
Similarity search loads all audio data into memory for processing, which can become a performance bottleneck with very large datasets.
Text search employs a naive ranking strategy, which may not yield optimal relevance for complex queries.
what_it_demonstrates: This project demonstrates the development of a RESTful API using FastAPI, integration of audio processing libraries like librosa for feature extraction, database management with SQLAlchemy and SQLite, implementation of similarity search algorithms (cosine, Euclidean distance) with feature normalization, handling file uploads, and a basic approach to natural language-based audio search using feature-to-label mapping. It showcases modular project structure and dependency management for a Python web service.
